seller-net-sheet.formula: commission = price*rate; transfer_tax = price*rate; tax_proration = annual_tax*days_seller_owes/365; net = price - payoff - commission - transfer_tax - fees - concessions - proration - other.
seller-net-sheet.edition: Per the TILA-RESPA Integrated Disclosure / Closing Disclosure (12 CFR 1026.38) and RESPA (12 CFR 1024), by name; the transfer-tax rate is state/local and user-supplied.
seller-net-sheet.freeAccess: Distinct from the buyer-side closing-costs tile. Estimate; the settlement statement and closing agent govern. Free at consumerfinance.gov and ecfr.gov.
seller-net-sheet.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
seller-net-sheet.editionNote: Transfer-tax base and payer vary by jurisdiction (some states levy per $500 of value). The proration convention (365 vs 360, arrears vs advance) varies.

assumptions.name: Payoff
assumptions.value: includes per-diem interest and any prepayment penalty not in the principal balance

two-stroke-mix-ratio-check.formula: ratio = fuel volume / oil volume (same units; 1 US gallon = 128 fl oz); oz per gallon = 128 / ratio; verdict vs the target ratio.
two-stroke-mix-ratio-check.edition: Two-stroke fuel/oil mix ratio check by volume, the inverse of the mix tile; first-principles volume arithmetic, public domain. The oil grade and ratio are set by the equipment manufacturer.
two-stroke-mix-ratio-check.freeAccess: Pure arithmetic, public; modern air-cooled two-strokes are commonly 50:1 with a JASO/ISO oil, but the equipment manual governs.
two-stroke-mix-ratio-check.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
two-stroke-mix-ratio-check.editionNote: The inverse of the two-stroke mix tile: from the fuel amount and the oil actually poured, the achieved gas:oil ratio is fuel volume / oil volume (both in the same units), compared against a target ratio. A LEAN mix (a higher X:1 than the target, too little oil) starves the crankshaft and rod bearings and is the dangerous error - it risks scoring or seizure; a RICH mix (a lower X:1, too much oil) smokes and fouls the plug but protects the engine. The ratio (50:1, 40:1, etc.) and oil specification come from the chainsaw / trimmer / outboard manual.

assumptions.name: Ratio by volume
assumptions.value: achieved ratio = fuel volume / oil volume, gas:oil by volume

assumptions.name: Lean vs rich
assumptions.value: a higher X:1 (lean) is the dangerous under-oiled error; a lower X:1 (rich) smokes but protects

thread-single-depth.formula: pitch_in = 1 / tpi; single_depth_in = 0.6134 x pitch_in (60-degree UN external thread height); compound_infeed_in = single_depth_in / cos(29.5 degrees).
thread-single-depth.edition: Single-point 60-degree (Unified/UN) external thread cutting depth and 29.5-degree compound infeed (Machinery's Handbook threading practice), by name; the thread standard, the tool geometry, and a thread gauge govern the finished part.
thread-single-depth.freeAccess: The thread-depth geometry (0.6134 x pitch for a UN external thread, and the 29.5-degree compound-infeed trig) is public machining practice; the threads-per-inch is the thread's spec.
thread-single-depth.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
thread-single-depth.editionNote: When a machinist cuts a screw thread on a lathe with a single-point 60-degree form tool, the tool must be fed in to a specific depth. The pitch of the thread is one divided by the threads per inch. For a Unified (UN) external thread, the height of the thread from crest to root is 0.6134 times the pitch; this comes from the geometry of the 60-degree fundamental triangle, whose sharp-V height is 0.86603 times the pitch, reduced by the standard truncation of the crest and root that the UN form specifies for the external thread. So a 1/2-13 thread has a pitch of 0.0769 inch and a radial thread depth of 0.6134 times 0.0769, or 0.0472 inch, and a coarser 3/4-10 is 0.0613 inch deep. In practice the tool is not fed straight in on the cross slide; instead the compound rest is set to 29.5 degrees, just under the 30-degree half-angle of the thread, so that as the compound advances the tool cuts almost entirely on the leading flank of the groove and merely skims the trailing flank, which produces a cleaner cut and longer tool life than plunging straight in. Because the compound feeds at that angle, it must travel farther than the straight radial depth: the compound infeed equals the radial depth divided by the cosine of 29.5 degrees, so the 1/2-13 thread needs 0.0472 divided by the cosine of 29.5, or 0.0542 inch, of compound travel. The depth is reached over several passes, with progressively lighter cuts near finish size, and the finished thread should be checked against a ring or thread gauge or by the three-wire measuring method rather than relying on the dialed depth alone, because tool wear, workpiece deflection, and the exact crest and root form all shift the actual fit. This is a lathe setup aid; the specific thread standard (UN, UNJ, or metric, which use slightly different truncations), the threading tool's geometry, and a thread gauge govern the finished part.

assumptions.name: UN external thread depth
assumptions.value: pitch = 1/TPI; external thread height = 0.6134 x pitch (60-degree UN truncation, from the 0.866 P sharp-V)

assumptions.name: Compound infeed
assumptions.value: compound set to 29.5 degrees; infeed = radial depth / cos(29.5) so the tool cuts on the leading flank; verify with a gauge / three-wire method

multi-load-vd.formula: Cumulative I × R per ordered segment; single-phase round-trip; allows mixed loads along one circuit.
multi-load-vd.edition: NEC 2023 (NFPA 70). Chapter 9 Tables 8 / 9; IEEE 141 by name.
multi-load-vd.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
multi-load-vd.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow NEC 2023. NEC 2026 is the current published edition; jurisdictions on NEC 2017 / 2020 / 2023 / 2026 use slightly different ambient corrections and ampacity ranges; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ.

assumptions.name: Round-trip factor
assumptions.value: 2× one-way length

combustion-lambda.formula: lambda = 20.9 / (20.9 - flue_o2_pct); excess_air_pct = (lambda - 1) x 100; afr_actual = lambda x afr_stoich(fuel).
combustion-lambda.edition: Combustion-analysis practice lambda and air-fuel ratio, by name.
combustion-lambda.freeAccess: The lambda and air-fuel-ratio relations are standard combustion-analysis practice; the analyzer and appliance manufacturer instructions govern the actual tune.
combustion-lambda.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
combustion-lambda.editionNote: Lambda is the same physics as excess air (lambda = 1 + excess_air/100), shown the way the instrument displays it. The air-fuel ratio is by mass; the stoichiometric ratio is a fuel property (17.2 natural gas, 15.5 propane, 14.5 #2 oil). The oxygen form assumes complete combustion, so measurable CO understates it; sample dry, air-free oxygen in the flue. The analyzer, the appliance, and the manufacturer instructions govern - a tuning aid, not a certified combustion test.

assumptions.name: Lambda from O2
assumptions.value: lambda = 20.9 / (20.9 - O2) = 1 + excess_air/100; the same physics excess-air-o2 reports

assumptions.name: Stoichiometric AFR
assumptions.value: by mass, 17.2 natural gas, 15.5 propane, 14.5 #2 oil

residential-framing.formula: Stud count = ceil(perimeter / stud_oc) + 8 (corner/T allowance). Plate lf = ceil(perimeter × 3 × 1.10) (sole + 2 top + 10% waste). Joist count = ceil(footprint / (joist_span × joist_oc)) + 2. Rafter count derived from approx_length / rafter_oc × 2 (both sides) + 2 (ridge ends). Rafter length = building_run × m_common where m_common = sqrt(P² + 144) / 12. Board feet per ft per nominal: 2x4 = 0.667, 2x6 = 1.0, 2x8 = 1.333, 2x10 = 1.667, 2x12 = 2.0.
residential-framing.edition: IRC 2021 (International Residential Code). Tables R502.5 (joists), R602.5 (studs), R802.5.1 (rafters). WWPA standard grading rules for board-feet conversions.
residential-framing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed structural engineer govern.
residential-framing.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow IRC 2021. Jurisdictions on IRC 2018 / 2024 differ at the margins; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ.

assumptions.name: Corner / T allowance
assumptions.value: +8 studs for a simple rectangle (engineering practice)

assumptions.name: Sizes
assumptions.value: stud 2x4 / joist 2x10 / rafter 2x8 (fixed in the page; selectable only through the API)

ssd-design-speed.formula: v is the positive root of 1.075 v^2 / (32.2 (f + g)) + 1.47 t_pr v - SSD = 0, i.e. v = (-b + sqrt(b^2 + 4 a SSD)) / (2 a) with a = 1.075/(32.2 (f+g)), b = 1.47 t_pr. The inverse of SSD = 1.47 t v + 1.075 v^2/(32.2 (f+g)), the Green Book form.
ssd-design-speed.edition: AASHTO Green Book (Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, 7th ed.) Chapter 3.
ssd-design-speed.freeAccess: transportation.org for TOC; AASHTO design SSD tables are licensed.
ssd-design-speed.governance: Math aid for personal verification. The ELD on the truck and the carrier tariff are the legal record. State limits may be lower than federal.
ssd-design-speed.editionNote: The fastest design speed a stretch of road can safely allow given the available stopping sight distance, the inverse of stopping-sight-distance: the speed is the positive root of the SSD quadratic. Use it to set a curve/crest advisory speed or to check whether a design speed is safe for the sight line to an intersection or over a hill. Braking distance grows with the square of speed while reaction distance grows linearly, so a modest sight-distance shortfall forces a larger speed cut than it seems; a downhill (negative) grade and wet/icy friction lower the safe speed further. This tile outputs the underlying physics; AASHTO design SSD tables round these numbers. A design aid, not a posted-speed determination; the state DOT governs roadway design.

assumptions.name: Friction coefficient
assumptions.value: 0.348 AASHTO design (11.2 ft/s^2 / 32.2, already a wet-pavement basis) / 0.20 poor wet surface or worn tires (not an AASHTO value) / 0.10 ice or packed snow
assumptions.source: AASHTO Green Book Chapter 3 for 0.348; engineering practice for 0.20 and 0.10

assumptions.name: Grade
assumptions.value: decimal; + uphill, - downhill lowers the safe speed

motor-run-hours-for-budget.formula: input_kW = HP x 0.746 x (load_factor/100) / (efficiency/100); max_hours = cost_budget / (input_kW x rate); annual_kWh = input_kW x max_hours. The inverse of annual_cost = input_kW x run_hours x rate.
motor-run-hours-for-budget.edition: First-principles electrical-input power and the 0.746 kW-per-HP identity, solved for the run hours.
motor-run-hours-for-budget.freeAccess: First-principles physics; no licensed source required.
motor-run-hours-for-budget.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
motor-run-hours-for-budget.editionNote: Single-edition (input power and energy cost are physical relations; the 0.746 constant is a fixed unit bridge), solved for the run hours a cost budget buys.

assumptions.name: Energy charge only
assumptions.value: the result is the energy-charge component only and excludes demand charges, time-of-use rates, and power-factor penalties, so the real hours before a bill target are fewer
assumptions.source: utility tariff governs the full bill

assumptions.name: Efficiency basis
assumptions.value: efficiency is the full-load efficiency; partial-load efficiency differs and the load factor scales the input power linearly as a first approximation

delta-wye-line-phase.formula: Wye: V_line = root-3 x V_phase, I_line = I_phase. Delta: V_line = V_phase, I_line = root-3 x I_phase. Connection-independent S = root-3 x V_line x I_line; P = S x PF. root-3 = 1.73205.
delta-wye-line-phase.edition: First-principles three-phase winding relations; classical balanced three-phase theory.
delta-wye-line-phase.freeAccess: First-principles physics; no licensed source required.
delta-wye-line-phase.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
delta-wye-line-phase.editionNote: Single-edition (the wye and delta line/phase relations and the root-3 power identity are physical relations).

assumptions.name: Balanced system
assumptions.value: the relations assume a balanced three-phase system; the root-3 factor is exact for balanced sinusoidal quantities

assumptions.name: Connection
assumptions.value: the equipment nameplate governs the actual connection (wye/star or delta)

drying-chamber-co2.formula: Q_fresh (cfm) = CO2 generation (cfm) x 1e6 / (C_indoor_ppm - C_outdoor_ppm); ACH = Q_fresh x 60 / containment_volume_ft3.
drying-chamber-co2.edition: ASHRAE 62.1 ventilation-rate mass-balance basis, by name.
drying-chamber-co2.freeAccess: ASHRAE-published; the steady-state mass balance is public. IICRC S500 governs the drying plan.
drying-chamber-co2.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
drying-chamber-co2.editionNote: Single-edition (steady-state single-zone CO2 mass balance; complements chamber-turnover, which sizes air movers not fresh air).

assumptions.name: Steady state
assumptions.value: well-mixed single zone at steady state; CO2 generation entered as cfm of CO2

refrigerant-charging.formula: Saturation T from bundled manufacturer P-T table by linear interpolation. Superheat = T_suction_line − T_sat(P_suction); Subcool = T_sat(P_liquid) − T_liquid_line. Each pressure input has a psig/psia toggle (psig is gauge default; psia adds 14.696 to psig).
refrigerant-charging.edition: Manufacturer-attributed P-T tables (DuPont, Honeywell Solstice, Chemours Opteon, Arkema Forane) by name; ASHRAE 34 safety classifications by name.
refrigerant-charging.freeAccess: Free at each manufacturer site; ASHRAE 34 read-only at ashrae.org.
refrigerant-charging.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed mechanical contractor govern. ACCA Manual J / D / S supersede rules of thumb.
refrigerant-charging.editionNote: Single-edition (manufacturer P-T tables; quarterly recheck per spec-v7 §8 cadence).

assumptions.name: Standard atmospheric pressure
assumptions.value: 14.696 psi (psig→psia conversion)

assumptions.name: Superheat target band
assumptions.value: 8-12 °F (manufacturer typical absent a charging chart)

assumptions.name: Subcool target band
assumptions.value: 8-15 °F (manufacturer typical absent a charging chart)

hydrostatic-test.formula: Test pressure: at least the working pressure for water systems (IPC 2021 Section 312.5; 1.5x is common engineering practice, not an IPC rule), and at least 1.5x the maximum working pressure but not less than 3 psig for fuel-gas systems (IFGC 2021 Section 406.4.1); recommended hold time scales with system volume.
hydrostatic-test.edition: IPC 2021 (International Plumbing Code). Section 312; IFGC 2021 (International Fuel Gas Code) / NFPA 54. Section 406.4.
hydrostatic-test.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed plumber / gas fitter govern. Verify against the IPC / IFGC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
hydrostatic-test.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow IPC 2021. Jurisdictions on IPC 2018 / 2024 differ in fixture-unit values and vent-sizing tables; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ. UPC-jurisdictions (CA, IN, MA, NV, parts of NJ) use the Uniform Plumbing Code instead. Editions available: bundled values follow IFGC 2021 / NFPA 54-2021. IFGC 2027 is the current published edition and 2024 preceded it; jurisdictions on any of these differ at the margins; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ.

assumptions.name: Default hold time
assumptions.value: ≥ 15 min for plumbing tests; ≥ 10 min for fuel-gas tests

grease-trap.formula: Volume = peak GPM × retention time × loading factor. Recommended nominal size is the next typical commercial trap size (20 to 3,000 gal). IPC 2021 Section 1003 governs interceptor selection.
grease-trap.edition: PDI G101 by name; IPC 2021 (International Plumbing Code). Section 1003.
grease-trap.freeAccess: Free read-only access at codes.iccsafe.org. PDI G101 licensed; manufacturer (Schier, Thermaco, Rockford) sizing tools free.
grease-trap.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed plumber / gas fitter govern. Verify against the IPC / IFGC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
grease-trap.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow IPC 2021. Jurisdictions on IPC 2018 / 2024 differ in fixture-unit values and vent-sizing tables; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ. UPC-jurisdictions (CA, IN, MA, NV, parts of NJ) use the Uniform Plumbing Code instead.

assumptions.name: Retention time
assumptions.value: 30 min unless user supplies

assumptions.name: Loading factor
assumptions.value: 1.25 unless user supplies a job-specific factor

square-footage.formula: Area = length × width (rectangle) and triangle / circle / sector for non-rectangular plans.
square-footage.edition: Classical geometry; IRC 2021 / IBC 2021 occupancy area definitions.
square-footage.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.

joist-deflection.formula: Mid-span deflection Δ = 5 × w × L⁴ / (384 × E × I) for uniformly loaded simple span. E and I are entered (take them from the AWC NDS Supplement design values and section properties for the species, grade and size).
joist-deflection.edition: AWC NDS-2018 (National Design Specification for Wood Construction). IRC 2021 (International Residential Code). §R301.7.
joist-deflection.freeAccess: Free at awc.org. Free read-only access at codes.iccsafe.org.
joist-deflection.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed structural engineer govern.
joist-deflection.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow IRC 2021. Jurisdictions on IRC 2018 / 2024 differ at the margins; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ.

assumptions.name: Section properties
assumptions.value: S4S actual dimensions per AWC NDS Supplement

confined-space-vent.formula: V = L * W * H (or operator-supplied volume). minutes_to_purge = V * N / Q. steady_ACH = Q * 60 / V. Default N (target air-changes) keyed to contaminant class: combustible-gas / oxygen-deficient / general = 7; H2S / CO = 10.
confined-space-vent.edition: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146 (Permit-Required Confined Spaces); NIOSH 80-106 (Working in Confined Spaces).
confined-space-vent.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed fire protection engineer govern.
confined-space-vent.editionNote: Companion to the v3 confined-space-purge tile. Adds L x W x H entry, contaminant-driven defaults, steady-state ACH, and the 1910.146(d)(5) 4-gas-meter reminder so the operator does not treat ventilation alone as space-certification.

assumptions.name: Default ACH targets
assumptions.value: combustible-gas / oxygen-deficient / general 7 ACH; H2S / CO 10 ACH
assumptions.source: NIOSH 80-106 typical and engineering practice for denser-than-air contaminants

assumptions.name: Pre-entry monitoring
assumptions.value: calibrated 4-gas meter readings before and during entry are required regardless of ventilation result

assumptions.name: Oxygen range
assumptions.value: O2 must be maintained between 19.5% and 23.5%

assumptions.name: Purge-time warning
assumptions.value: purge time above 60 minutes surfaces a higher-capacity-blower hint

assumptions.name: Steady-ACH floor
assumptions.value: steady-state ACH below 6 surfaces a 'verify blower placement / path length' warning per NIOSH 80-106 typical minimum

overtime.formula: Regular pay = min(hours, 40) × rate. OT = max(hours − 40, 0) × rate × 1.5 per FLSA 29 USC 207, up to the double-time threshold; hours past that threshold (default 60) pay the double-time multiple. The FLSA has no double time -- set the threshold above the week's hours for a pure FLSA figure; double time is a contract or state rule (California's is DAILY, past 12 h). The regular rate must include non-discretionary bonuses (29 CFR 778.110(b)); enter that rate. Some states (CA, AK, NV) require daily OT.
overtime.edition: Fair Labor Standards Act 29 USC 207 by section. State daily-OT rules per CA Labor Code §510, AK Stat §23.10.060, NV Admin Code §608.140.
overtime.freeAccess: 29 USC 207 free at uscode.house.gov; state codes free at each state legislature site.
overtime.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
overtime.editionNote: Single-edition (FLSA 29 USC 207 as currently codified). State daily-OT rules vary.

assumptions.name: FLSA threshold
assumptions.value: 40 hr/week federal; state daily thresholds may apply (CA / AK / NV 8 hr/day)

anhydrous-ammonia-rate.formula: product_lb_per_ac = n_target_lb_per_ac / 0.82; product_gal_per_ac = product_lb_per_ac / 5.15; acres_per_tank = tank_gal / product_gal_per_ac.
anhydrous-ammonia-rate.edition: Anhydrous ammonia fertilizer grade (82-0-0) and liquid density (~5.15 lb/gal), by name; extension-service and co-op practice. The soil-test N recommendation and the label govern.
anhydrous-ammonia-rate.freeAccess: The grade (82% N) and the liquid density are public product facts; the target N comes from the soil-test recommendation and the tank size from the equipment.
anhydrous-ammonia-rate.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
anhydrous-ammonia-rate.editionNote: Anhydrous ammonia (NH3) is the highest-analysis nitrogen fertilizer, graded 82-0-0 -- 82% nitrogen by weight. So the product needed to deliver a target N rate is the target divided by 0.82, and at a liquid density of about 5.15 lb/gal that converts to gallons per acre; a nurse tank's usable gallons divided by the per-acre gallons is the acres it covers before a refill. Anhydrous is a compressed, refrigerated-when-released, and acutely hazardous liquid: it must be applied with a properly calibrated, flow-monitored applicator (temperature and flashing vapor affect the metered rate), and handled with the required PPE, a water source, and closed-transfer / anti-drift precautions per the label and the applicator's certification. This is a rate estimate; the applicator calibration, the certified soil-test nitrogen recommendation, and the co-op / product label govern the actual application. This is distinct from a multi-nutrient NPK blend, which solves a soil test into urea, DAP, and potash.

assumptions.name: Grade and density
assumptions.value: 82-0-0 (82% N); ~5.15 lb/gal liquid; product = N/0.82, gal/ac = lb/ac / 5.15

assumptions.name: Calibration and safety
assumptions.value: flow-monitored, calibrated applicator; PPE, water, closed transfer per the label; the certification governs

pearson-correlation.formula: Pearson r = sum((x - xbar)(y - ybar)) / sqrt(sum(x - xbar)^2 * sum(y - ybar)^2). R^2 = r^2. Significance test for rho = 0: t = r * sqrt(n - 2) / sqrt(1 - r^2) on n - 2 degrees of freedom; two-tailed p = 2 * (1 - tcdf(|t|, n - 2)).
pearson-correlation.edition: OpenIntro Statistics 4th ed. Chapter 8 (introduction to linear regression) by name; the Student-t CDF via the regularized incomplete beta function per Numerical Recipes in C 2nd ed. §6.4.
pearson-correlation.freeAccess: OpenIntro Statistics free at openintro.org; Numerical Recipes chapters free at numerical.recipes.
pearson-correlation.governance: Estimate only. Readability formulas and similar metrics are derived from a representative population and have known edge-case noise. The classroom teacher governs final text selection, grade placement, and assessment decisions.
pearson-correlation.editionNote: Correlation is not causation; a strong r can arise from a lurking variable or a non-linear relationship that the linear coefficient cannot see. The significance test assumes approximately bivariate-normal data; inspect a scatter plot for small samples.

assumptions.name: Degrees of freedom
assumptions.value: n - 2 (two parameters estimated)
assumptions.source: Student-t test for a correlation coefficient

assumptions.name: Student-t CDF
assumptions.value: derived from the regularized incomplete beta function I_x(df/2, 1/2)

rooftop-temp-adder.formula: adder = 60 F (33 C) where height above roof < 7/8 in (0.875 in), else 0; design_ambient = measured + adder; corrected = base_ampacity x (90 C-column correction factor at the design ambient).
rooftop-temp-adder.edition: Raceways and cables exposed to sunlight on or above rooftops, NEC 2020/2023 310.15(B)(2), with the 310.15(B)(1) 90 C-column ambient correction, by name.
rooftop-temp-adder.freeAccess: NEC is free to read at nfpa.org/freeaccess. The 2017 NEC reduced the older tiered table to this single 33 C adder applied below 7/8 in; standoffs at or above 7/8 in remove it.
rooftop-temp-adder.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
rooftop-temp-adder.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow NEC 2023. NEC 2026 is the current published edition; jurisdictions on NEC 2017 / 2020 / 2023 / 2026 use slightly different ambient corrections and ampacity ranges; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ.

assumptions.name: Sunlight adder
assumptions.value: 33 C (60 F) added to the outdoor ambient where the raceway is less than 7/8 in above the roof

assumptions.name: Correction basis
assumptions.value: the 90 C-column temperature-correction factor applied to the corrected ambient

pressure-tank-drawdown.formula: Diaphragm-tank drawdown by Boyle's law on absolute pressures: drawdown = V_tank * (P_pre_abs/P_in_abs - P_pre_abs/P_out_abs), P_abs = P_gauge + 14.7, precharge ~ cut-in - 2 psi. Runtime = drawdown / pump_gpm; size mode inverts for V_tank.
pressure-tank-drawdown.edition: Pressure-tank drawdown from Boyle's law on the diaphragm air charge and the anti-short-cycle minimum-runtime rule (about 1 min per cycle), per the published pump/tank engineering practice (Amtrol/WellMate and the WQA references), by name; first-principles gas law.
pressure-tank-drawdown.freeAccess: First-principles gas law. The pump manufacturer's minimum runtime and the installed precharge govern.
pressure-tank-drawdown.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed plumber / gas fitter govern. Verify against the IPC / IFGC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
pressure-tank-drawdown.editionNote: Single-edition (Boyle's law). Precharge defaults to cut-in minus 2 psi, the standard diaphragm-tank rule, and is flagged.

assumptions.name: Precharge
assumptions.value: cut-in minus 2 psi unless overridden; a precharge AT cut-in gives the maximum drawdown (Amtrol), while one ABOVE cut-in leaves the tank empty before the pump starts

curb-gutter-volume.formula: volume_cy = cross_section_ft2 x length_ft / 27 x (1 + waste_pct/100); cy_per_100lf = cross_section_ft2 x 100 / 27.
curb-gutter-volume.edition: Linear-pour identity by name (fixed cross-section over a run to cubic yards, plus the per-100-LF ordering rate); first-principles volume arithmetic.
curb-gutter-volume.freeAccess: The volume arithmetic is public first-principles; the cross-section comes from the standard curb-and-gutter detail (no copyrighted section reproduced).
curb-gutter-volume.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
curb-gutter-volume.editionNote: The cross-sectional area comes from the DOT or municipal standard curb-and-gutter detail (the user computes or measures it). The cy per 100 LF is the ordering rule of thumb. A linear per-station pour distinct from the shape presets in concrete.

assumptions.name: Cross-section
assumptions.value: from the DOT or municipal standard curb-and-gutter detail (measured or computed)

assumptions.name: Ordering rate
assumptions.value: cy per 100 LF = cross-section x 100 / 27 (rule of thumb)

pv-ac-output-circuit.formula: continuous_current_a = ac_power_w / (ac_voltage_v x [1 single-phase, sqrt(3) three-phase]); min_conductor_ampacity_a = 1.25 x continuous_current_a; ocpd_a = next standard size (NEC 240.6) >= 1.25 x continuous_current_a.
pv-ac-output-circuit.edition: NEC 690.8(B) (continuous current), 705.60 (interconnected-source overcurrent), 240.4 (conductor protection), and 240.6 (standard OCPD sizes), by name; the inverter datasheet and the AHJ govern.
pv-ac-output-circuit.freeAccess: The output-current relation is power / voltage (public); the 125% continuous factor and the standard OCPD sizes are public NEC, and the inverter power, voltage, and phase come from the datasheet.
pv-ac-output-circuit.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
pv-ac-output-circuit.editionNote: The inverter AC output circuit -- the conductors and overcurrent device from a PV or ESS inverter to its point of connection. The inverter's rated continuous output current is its AC output power divided by the output voltage, times sqrt(3) for a three-phase inverter. Because the inverter is a continuous source, NEC 690.8(B) / 705.60 / 240.4 size both the conductor and the overcurrent device at 125% of that current, and 240.6 rounds the OCPD up to the next standard size. Where the datasheet gives a rated maximum continuous AC output current, use it (it can differ slightly from power / voltage). The point of connection to a busbar or panel is separately limited by the 705.12 busbar rules (the 120% allowance or a supply-side connection), checked with pv-interconnection-busbar. This is distinct from the DC-side conductor sizing (pv-circuit-ampacity, the 690.8(A) 156% rule on Isc). A sizing estimate; the inverter datasheet, the AHJ, and the adopted NEC edition govern the final design.

assumptions.name: 125% continuous
assumptions.value: conductor and OCPD at 1.25 x the continuous output current; OCPD to the next standard size (240.6)

assumptions.name: Busbar limit separate
assumptions.value: the 705.12 point-of-connection / busbar limit is checked separately (pv-interconnection-busbar)

dewatering-rate.formula: drawdown_gal = pit_len x pit_wid x drawdown x 7.48052; pump_gpm = drawdown_gal / drawdown_min + inflow; sized_gpm = pump_gpm x (1 + safety/100).
dewatering-rate.edition: First-principles volume and pumping-rate arithmetic by name; defers total dynamic head to the pump-tdh tile.
dewatering-rate.freeAccess: The 7.48 gal/ft^3 constant is exact and public. The inflow must be estimated from a pumping test.
dewatering-rate.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
dewatering-rate.editionNote: The inflow is the number that actually matters and must be estimated from the soil, head, and a pumping test, not guessed. Discharge water is managed for sediment and permitted discharge. Dewatering changes effective stress and can destabilize the wall - a competent-person and engineering call.

assumptions.name: Volume constant
assumptions.value: 7.48052 gal per ft^3 (exact)

assumptions.name: Safety margin
assumptions.value: 25% pump-sizing margin (default)

barrel-volume.formula: Parabolic staves V = (pi L/15)(2D^2 + Dd + 3/4 d^2) (exact for a parabolic profile); circular-arc staves V = (pi L/12)(2D^2 + d^2) (Kepler); both collapse to the cylinder when D = d.
barrel-volume.edition: The barrel / cask volume - standard solid geometry (Kepler's barrel rule) as in Machinery's Handbook (Industrial Press), by name; public domain.
barrel-volume.freeAccess: Pure solid geometry, public; the bung diameter, head diameter, and length are user-supplied.
barrel-volume.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
barrel-volume.editionNote: Volume of a barrel or cask - the bulged-side shape a straight-wall cylinder tile cannot give: a barrel, cask, bulged steel drum, or rain barrel that swells to a larger middle (bung) diameter D than its ends (head diameter d) over a length L. Two standard closed forms bracket it: parabolic staves V = (pi L/15)(2D^2 + Dd + 3/4 d^2), exact when the stave profile is a parabola, and spheroidal staves V = (pi L/12)(2D^2 + d^2), the exact frustum of a prolate spheroid (the excise 'first variety' cask); true circular-arc staves read slightly below it. A real barrel's staves fall between the two, typically under 1% apart, so the pair brackets the true volume. Both reduce exactly to the straight cylinder pi(D/2)^2 L when D = d. Enter inside dimensions in inches; reported in US gallons and cubic feet. The staved geometry is idealized; a strapping chart or a water fill governs custody transfer.

assumptions.name: Parabolic staves
assumptions.value: V = (pi L/15)(2D^2 + Dd + 3/4 d^2), exact for a parabolic profile

assumptions.name: Circular staves
assumptions.value: V = (pi L/12)(2D^2 + d^2), Kepler's barrel rule

assumptions.name: Scope
assumptions.value: bung diameter >= head diameter (bulges outward); both forms collapse to the cylinder when D = d

engine-bmep.formula: BMEP(psi) = 150.8 x torque(lb-ft) / displacement(CID) for a 4-stroke (75.4 for a 2-stroke); from BMEP = 2*pi*n_rev*T/V_d with T in lb-in and V_d in in^3.
engine-bmep.edition: Brake mean effective pressure (SAE; Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals), by name; the engine and its dyno sheet govern.
engine-bmep.freeAccess: BMEP's definition (work per displacement per cycle) is standard engine theory; the torque and displacement come from the dyno sheet and the engine spec.
engine-bmep.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
engine-bmep.editionNote: Brake mean effective pressure normalizes torque by displacement -- the average pressure that, acting on the piston through one power stroke, would produce the measured torque -- so it strips out engine SIZE and measures how hard each cycle works, letting engines of any displacement be compared directly. From Power = 2*pi*N*T and Power = BMEP x V_d x (N / n_rev), BMEP = 2*pi*n_rev*T/V_d, which with torque in lb-ft and displacement in cubic inches is 150.8 x T/CID for a 4-stroke (n_rev = 2) and 75.4 for a 2-stroke (n_rev = 1). It is evaluated at the torque peak, not peak power. Naturally-aspirated gasoline engines top out around 180-190 psi because they fill on a single atmosphere, so a higher BMEP is the signature of boost and a low one points to a mild cam, a restriction, or wear. Use the peak torque from a corrected dyno pull. A comparison metric, not a design limit.

assumptions.name: Cycle factor
assumptions.value: 150.8 for a 4-stroke (fires every 2 crank revs), 75.4 for a 2-stroke (every rev)

assumptions.name: Evaluated at torque peak
assumptions.value: BMEP is taken at the rpm of maximum torque, using a standard-day corrected dyno figure

sailboat-performance-ratios.formula: displaced_volume_ft3 = displacement_lb / 64; sa_d_ratio = sail_area_sqft / displaced_volume_ft3^(2/3); dl_ratio = (displacement_lb / 2240) / (0.01 x lwl_ft)^3.
sailboat-performance-ratios.edition: Sailboat performance ratios (sail area-to-displacement and displacement-to-length; Skene's Elements of Yacht Design; Gerr, The Nature of Boats), by name; the loaded displacement, the measured sail area and waterline, and a naval architect's velocity-prediction analysis govern real performance.
sailboat-performance-ratios.freeAccess: The two ratios are public yacht-design practice; the sail area, displacement, and waterline length are the boat's published or measured particulars.
sailboat-performance-ratios.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
sailboat-performance-ratios.editionNote: Two long-standing dimensionless ratios let a surveyor, designer, or buyer size up a sailboat's character straight from its specifications. The sail area-to-displacement ratio, SA/D, is the sail area divided by the boat's displaced volume raised to the two-thirds power; the displaced volume in cubic feet is the displacement in pounds divided by 64, the weight of a cubic foot of seawater. Because it compares a sail area to a volume-to-the-two-thirds (which has the units of area), the ratio is dimensionless and expresses how much driving sail the boat carries for its size -- effectively its power-to-weight. A value under about 16 marks a heavy, under-canvassed cruiser, 16 to 20 a moderate cruiser, and over 20 a performance boat or an outright racer. The displacement-to-length ratio, DLR, is the displacement expressed in long tons of 2,240 pounds, divided by the cube of one one-hundredth of the waterline length in feet; it captures how heavy the boat is for its sailing length. Under 100 is an ultralight, 100 to 200 light, 200 to 300 moderate, and over 300 a heavy, full-keel cruiser. A boat with 500 square feet of sail, 10,000 pounds of displacement, and a 30-foot waterline has an SA/D of 500 divided by (10,000 over 64) to the two-thirds, about 17.2, a moderate cruiser, and a DLR of (10,000 over 2,240) divided by 0.30 cubed, about 165, on the light side. A larger rig or a lighter hull raises the SA/D; a heavier boat on a shorter waterline raises the DLR. These are comparative screens for ranking boats, not a performance prediction; the actual displacement in loaded versus design trim, the true measured sail area and waterline length, and a naval architect's velocity-prediction program govern how the boat really sails.

assumptions.name: SA/D and DLR
assumptions.value: SA/D = sail area / (disp/64)^(2/3); DLR = (disp/2240) / (0.01 x LWL)^3; 64 lb/ft^3 seawater, 2240 lb/long ton

assumptions.name: Interpretation bands
assumptions.value: SA/D <16 heavy, 16-20 moderate, >20 performance; DLR <100 ultralight, 100-200 light, 200-300 moderate, >300 heavy; comparative screens, not a VPP

excavation-protection-trigger.formula: a means of egress is required where depth >= 4 ft, within 25 ft of lateral travel, so with each point serving 25 ft in each direction the count is max(1, ceil(trench length / 50)); cave-in protection is required unless the excavation is entirely in stable rock OR depth < 5 ft AND a competent person has examined the ground with no indication of a potential cave-in.
excavation-protection-trigger.edition: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.651(c)(2) and 1926.652(a)(1), Subpart P - Excavations. US federal regulations in the public domain, quoted directly.
excavation-protection-trigger.freeAccess: 29 CFR is published in full at no cost by OSHA and the eCFR.
excavation-protection-trigger.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
excavation-protection-trigger.editionNote: The finding is that the two triggers sit at different depths and in the order most people carry them backwards. The ACCESS rule bites first, at 4 ft: a stairway, ladder, ramp, or other safe means of egress in trench excavations 4 feet or more in depth, so as to require no more than 25 feet of lateral travel. The CAVE-IN rule bites at 5 ft. So a 4.5 ft trench needs a ladder and may need no shoring at all - and it is common to hear the shallower number attached to the shoring instead. The second trap is inside the shallow exception, which has TWO conditions rather than one: less than 5 ft in depth AND examination of the ground by a competent person providing no indication of a potential cave-in. Depth alone exempts nothing, so an unexamined 4 ft trench still requires a protective system, and the tile calls that case out by name rather than reporting a bare not-required. The 25 ft is LATERAL TRAVEL measured along the trench to the point of egress - not a straight line and not a diagonal climb out - and it is travel for someone who may be moving away from a collapse, which is why the number is small. Because each point serves 25 ft in each direction, one ladder covers 50 ft of run, so the count over a long trench is a spacing problem rather than a single-ladder problem. Not checked: WHICH protective system is appropriate and its design under 652(b) or (c) - the trench-slope and excavation-bench-plan tiles handle sloping and benching geometry once the requirement is established; soil classification, which drives all of it; any registered-professional-engineer approval that the deeper design options carry, which is a separate determination in the design paragraphs and is deliberately not asserted here; the daily and after-event inspections a competent person owes; water accumulation, adjacent structures, and underground installations; atmospheric testing; and the spoil-pile setback, which has its own tile. A screen, not an excavation plan; Subpart P and the competent person govern.

assumptions.name: Egress trigger
assumptions.value: trench excavations 4 ft or more in depth

assumptions.name: Lateral travel
assumptions.value: no more than 25 ft, measured along the trench

assumptions.name: Point spacing
assumptions.value: each point serves 25 ft each way, so one covers 50 ft of run

assumptions.name: Cave-in trigger
assumptions.value: required unless entirely in stable rock, or under 5 ft AND examined

assumptions.name: Two conditions
assumptions.value: the shallow exception needs both depth and examination - depth alone exempts nothing

assumptions.name: Not determined
assumptions.value: which protective system, soil class, PE approval, inspections, water, utilities

was-srt-control.formula: system_solids = V x MLSS x 8.34; solids_to_waste = system_solids / SRT; effluent_solids = Qeff x TSSeff x 8.34; Q_WAS = (solids_to_waste - effluent_solids) / (WAS x 8.34); Q_WAS_gpm = Q_WAS x 1e6 / 1440.
was-srt-control.edition: WAS rate for a target SRT (MCRT/SRT control; WEF operator training), by name.
was-srt-control.freeAccess: The SRT-control solids-balance relation is a public wastewater-operations method; the process trend and the operator govern the actual set point.
was-srt-control.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
was-srt-control.editionNote: This is the inverse of a sludge-age readout - it answers how much to waste today. SRT responds over roughly one SRT (days), so over-correcting on a single reading chases the process; make changes gradually. The effluent solids carried over the weir count as wasted and reduce the WAS pump rate. An operating aid, not a process design.

assumptions.name: Solids to waste
assumptions.value: solids_to_waste = system_solids / SRT; the effluent solids reduce the required WAS pumping

assumptions.name: Slow response
assumptions.value: SRT reacts over roughly one SRT; change the wasting gradually rather than chasing a single reading

cabinet-linear-feet.formula: base LF = wall run - appliance openings - (corners x cabinet depth); filler = corners x filler width; wall and tall LF taken as entered; cabinet count = ceil(LF x 12 / standard width); countertop LF = base LF + corner length; toe kick = base + tall LF.
cabinet-linear-feet.edition: Cabinet takeoff arithmetic - no standard claimed and no manufacturer size table reproduced.
cabinet-linear-feet.freeAccess: Counting arithmetic; nominal cabinet sizes are published free in every manufacturer's catalog.
cabinet-linear-feet.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
cabinet-linear-feet.editionNote: Each inside corner eats one cabinet DEPTH off one of its two legs, because the two runs cannot both occupy the corner - that is why an L-kitchen measured wall-to-wall always over-counts, and it is the arithmetic this tile exists to get right. Appliance openings come OUT of the base run and fillers go IN; order the filler even when the arithmetic closes, because it absorbs out-of-square walls and gives door and drawer clearance at corners and end walls. Base, wall, and tall runs are kept separate because they price differently per foot. Cabinet counts assume every box is the standard width entered - a real elevation mixes widths, so treat the count as a check on the linear feet, not as an order. Countertop runs the FULL corner unlike the cabinets, so it is reported with the corner length added back. The shop drawing and the manufacturer's nominal sizes govern.

assumptions.name: Corner rule
assumptions.value: one cabinet depth is lost per inside corner, from one leg only

assumptions.name: Counts are a check
assumptions.value: boxes assume the single standard width entered; real elevations mix widths

assumptions.name: Countertop differs
assumptions.value: the top runs the full corner, so corner length is added back for it

steel-cb.formula: Cb = 12.5 Mmax / (2.5 Mmax + 3 MA + 4 MB + 3 MC), absolute moments at the max and the quarter (MA), mid (MB), and three-quarter (MC) points of the unbraced segment; Rm = 1 (doubly symmetric).
steel-cb.edition: The AISC 360-22 Eq. F1-1 lateral-torsional-buckling moment-gradient factor Cb, by name.
steel-cb.freeAccess: AISC 360 is free to read at aisc.org (Specification for Structural Steel Buildings); Eq. F1-1 is in Chapter F. The four segment moments are the user's own analysis results.
steel-cb.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
steel-cb.editionNote: The AISC 360-22 Eq. F1-1 lateral-torsional-buckling moment-gradient factor Cb, the value the steel-beam-ltb tile takes as an input but defaults to a conservative 1.0: Cb = 12.5 Mmax / (2.5 Mmax + 3 MA + 4 MB + 3 MC), using the ABSOLUTE moments at the maximum and at the quarter (MA), mid (MB), and three-quarter (MC) points of the unbraced segment, with Rm = 1.0 for a doubly symmetric member. It rewards a moment diagram that is not uniform: uniform moment (equal end moments in single curvature) gives Cb = 1.0, a simple-span uniformly loaded beam braced only at its ends gives 1.14, and a diagram peaked near midspan with light quarter-point moments goes higher -- each a direct multiplier on the LTB nominal moment Mn (capped at Mp). Because Mmax is the largest moment in the segment, Cb is at least 1.0. Take Cb = 1.0 for a cantilever with a free unbraced end, and recompute for each unbraced segment. A design aid, not a substitute for the structural engineer of record.

assumptions.name: Moment-gradient factor
assumptions.value: Cb = 12.5 Mmax / (2.5 Mmax + 3 MA + 4 MB + 3 MC)

assumptions.name: Absolute moments
assumptions.value: MA, MB, MC at the 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 points of the unbraced segment; Rm = 1 for a doubly symmetric shape

assumptions.name: Bounds
assumptions.value: uniform moment -> 1.0; Cb >= 1.0 since Mmax is the segment maximum; feeds steel-beam-ltb
assumptions.source: AISC 360-22 F1 / scope of this tile

asce7-load-combinations.formula: combos = [D; D+L; D+kS; D+0.75L+0.75kS; D+0.6W; D+0.75L+0.75(0.6W)+0.75kS; 0.6D+0.6W], k = 0.7 for an ASCE 7-22 snow load, 1.0 for a 7-16 snow or roof live / rain; governing_gravity = max(combos); controlling_case = min(combos); net_uplift = controlling_case < 0 ? -controlling_case : 0.
asce7-load-combinations.edition: ASCE 7-22 §2.4.1 basic ASD load combinations (2024 IBC), by name, with the 7-16 snow factor of 1.0 available for a service-level snow.
asce7-load-combinations.freeAccess: The basic ASD load combinations are stated in ASCE 7 §2.4.1; the arithmetic is public.
asce7-load-combinations.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
asce7-load-combinations.editionNote: The ASCE 7-22 §2.4.1 basic ASD load combinations: D; D+L; D+(Lr or 0.7S or R); D+0.75L+0.75(Lr or 0.7S or R); D+0.6W; D+0.75L+0.75(0.6W)+0.75(Lr or 0.7S or R); 0.6D+0.6W. ASCE 7-22 made snow strength-level (the LRFD snow factor fell to 1.0), so its ASD combinations take 0.7S; ASCE 7-16's service-level snow took 1.0, and applying 0.7 to it would be 30% unconservative, so the roof-load type is an input. This is the basic ASD set (the seismic E combinations and the LRFD strength set are a separate selection); the roof load entered as S stands in for the governing of roof-live / snow / rain; the dead load in the 0.6D combinations is the reliably-present dead only. Wind is signed (positive downward, negative uplift). A load-combination aid, not a member design.

assumptions.name: Snow factor
assumptions.value: 0.7S for an ASCE 7-22 (strength-level) snow; 1.0 for a 7-16 (service-level) snow or for Lr or R
assumptions.source: ASCE 7-22 §2.4.1; ICC, Demystifying Loads (2024 IBC / ASCE 7-22)

assumptions.name: Governing gravity
assumptions.value: the largest of the seven combinations is the downward demand that sizes the member

assumptions.name: Net uplift
assumptions.value: when 0.6D + 0.6W (or another case) goes below zero, the magnitude is the uplift the connection must resist

assumptions.name: Signed wind
assumptions.value: wind is entered signed: positive downward (pressure), negative upward (uplift)

required-section-modulus.formula: LRFD: Zx_req = 12 Mu / (0.90 Fy); ASD: Zx_req = 12 (1.67) Ma / Fy (in^3, the 12 converts kip-ft to kip-in).
required-section-modulus.edition: AISC 360-22 Chapter F (F2.1) Mp = Fy Zx and the §B3 resistance/safety factors, inverted for the required plastic section modulus, by name.
required-section-modulus.freeAccess: The Mp = Fy Zx relation and the Omega_b / phi_b factors are stated in AISC 360, whose provisions are published; inverting them for the required Zx is public arithmetic.
required-section-modulus.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
required-section-modulus.editionNote: The AISC 360-22 Chapter F plastic-moment relation Mp = Fy Zx inverted for the required plastic section modulus of a compact, laterally-braced beam: LRFD phi_b Mn >= Mu with phi_b = 0.90 gives Zx >= 12 Mu / (0.90 Fy); ASD Mn / Omega_b >= Ma with Omega_b = 1.67 gives Zx >= 12 (1.67) Ma / Fy (the 12 converts kip-ft to kip-in). The designer selects the lightest W-shape whose Zx meets or exceeds the result, exactly as the forward flexural-capacity tile takes Zx as an input. This assumes a compact section fully braced against lateral-torsional buckling (Lb <= Lp, Mn = Mp); a noncompact flange or an unbraced length reduces the capacity (F3 / F2.2) and needs its own check. A design aid, not a substitute for the engineer of record.

assumptions.name: Inverse of the forward tile
assumptions.value: Zx_req solves phi_b Fy Zx / 12 = Mu (LRFD) or Fy Zx / (12 Omega_b) = Ma (ASD); feeding it into steel-beam-flexure returns the demand

assumptions.name: Compact + braced
assumptions.value: Mn = Mp = Fy Zx (the plastic plateau); a noncompact or unbraced beam needs the F3 / F2.2 lateral-torsional-buckling check

liquefaction-screening.formula: rd = 1 - 0.00233172 z (z <= 30.02 ft), 1.174 - 0.00813816 z (to 75.46 ft), 0.744 - 0.0024384 z (to 98.43 ft), else 0.5; CSR = 0.65 amax (sigma_v/sigma'_v) rd; FS = (CRR/CSR) MSF; liquefiable if FS < 1.
liquefaction-screening.edition: The Seed-Idriss simplified liquefaction-triggering procedure (NCEER/NSF workshop consensus), by name.
liquefaction-screening.freeAccess: The Seed-Idriss simplified CSR/CRR procedure and the rd relation are standard published earthquake-geotechnical results.
liquefaction-screening.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
liquefaction-screening.editionNote: The Seed-Idriss simplified liquefaction-triggering screen: the stress-reduction coefficient rd = 1 - 0.00233172 z for a depth z <= 30.02 ft, 1.174 - 0.00813816 z to 75.46 ft, 0.744 - 0.0024384 z to 98.43 ft, and 0.5 below that (Youd et al. 2001; the published per-meter constants 0.00765, 0.0267 and 0.008 and the 9.15, 23 and 30 m breakpoints restated per foot via 0.3048), the earthquake-induced cyclic stress ratio CSR = 0.65 amax (sigma_v / sigma'_v) rd, and the factor of safety FS = (CRR / CSR) x MSF, with liquefaction triggered when FS < 1. The cyclic resistance ratio CRR is read from the (N1)60 or CPT charts for the sand, and the magnitude scaling factor MSF adjusts from the Mw 7.5 reference event. This is a screening tool for level ground; a site-specific triggering analysis, the fines-content correction, the overburden correction, and the post-liquefaction settlement/lateral-spread evaluation are the geotechnical engineer's work. A design aid; the geotechnical engineer of record governs.

assumptions.name: Cyclic stress ratio
assumptions.value: CSR = 0.65 amax (sigma_v/sigma'_v) rd

assumptions.name: Factor of safety
assumptions.value: FS = (CRR/CSR) x MSF; liquefiable if FS < 1

assumptions.name: Screening only
assumptions.value: level ground; fines/overburden corrections and settlement are separate

masonry-lintel-loading.formula: tri_h = span/2; arching when wall_above >= tri_h + 8 in: W = 0.5 x span x tri_h x wall_psf and the moment-equivalent UDL = 4 W / (3 x span); otherwise W = span x wall_above x wall_psf (full rectangle) and UDL = W/span.
masonry-lintel-loading.edition: The masonry arching-action lintel-load method (TMS 402 commentary / masonry design references), by name.
masonry-lintel-loading.freeAccess: The 45-degree arching triangle for masonry lintel loads is a standard masonry-design method (TMS 402 commentary / masonry design references). The engineer of record governs.
masonry-lintel-loading.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
masonry-lintel-loading.editionNote: Masonry lintel arching load: for masonry above an opening, the lintel carries only the triangular dead load within a 45-degree triangle (height = span/2) IF enough wall is above (wall above >= span/2 + 8 in, NCMA TEK 17-1), W = 0.5 x span x (span/2) x wall psf, a moment-equivalent UDL of 4W/(3 x span) (W/span matches the end shear but understates the moment 25%). NCMA TEK 17-01D's own worked example loads the triangle to 3.5 ft (half span plus the 8 in), which reads about 25% more moment than its text's half-span triangle; this follows the text and BIA Technical Note 31B. If the wall above is shorter than the triangle plus 8 in (a lintel near the top of the wall or under a beam bearing), arching is not developed and the lintel carries the full rectangle span x height x psf - MORE load than the arched case. This returns the dead load only: add the floor/roof/superimposed loads within the triangle separately, and confirm the arching assumptions (bond, no control joint in the triangle). A design aid; the engineer of record governs.

assumptions.name: Arching triangle
assumptions.value: 45-degree triangle, height span/2; arches only when wall above >= span/2 + 8 in (TEK 17-1: 8 in of wall above the apex)

assumptions.name: No arching case
assumptions.value: insufficient wall above -> the full rectangle span x height x psf (more load)

assumptions.name: Dead load only
assumptions.value: add floor/roof/superimposed loads separately; confirm bond and no control joint

steam-trap-sizing.formula: condensate_lbhr = heat_duty_btuhr / hfg_btulb; req_capacity_lbhr = condensate_lbhr x safety_factor (2x typical, 3x warm-up / modulating).
steam-trap-sizing.edition: First-principles condensate-load relation and the safety-factor practice, by name; the latent heat is from the ASME steam tables. Not edition-bound.
steam-trap-sizing.freeAccess: The condensate load is the heat duty divided by the published latent heat at the operating pressure; the safety factor is standard practice.
steam-trap-sizing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
steam-trap-sizing.editionNote: Single-edition (the relation and the safety-factor practice do not roll). The trap is SELECTED FROM THE MANUFACTURER'S CAPACITY CHART at the actual differential pressure the installation develops - this tile gives the load and the capacity target, not a trap model, and modulating, warm-up, and stall conditions can demand a larger factor or a different trap type.

assumptions.name: Latent heat
assumptions.value: hfg from the saturated-steam table at the operating pressure, entered, or computed from an entered gauge pressure by IAPWS-IF97 on a 14.696 psia atmosphere

assumptions.name: Safety factor
assumptions.value: 2x typical, 3x on warm-up / modulating service; higher factors for stall conditions

assumptions.name: Selection
assumptions.value: the trap is sized from the manufacturer's capacity chart at the actual differential pressure

turbine-density-correction.formula: the ISA barometric relation: density = reference density x 518.67 / (459.67 + degF) x (1 - 6.8754e-6 x elevation) raised to 5.2559; power scales LINEARLY with the density ratio below rated, and the IEC method instead scales the measured wind speed by the cube root of that ratio.
turbine-density-correction.edition: The ISA barometric density relation by name against the IEC/ISO reference of 0.0765 lb/cu ft at 59 degF and sea level, with the IEC 61400-12 cube-root wind-speed correction named. The turbine manufacturer's power curve, its stated reference conditions and correction method, and IEC 61400-12 govern.
turbine-density-correction.freeAccess: A density ratio from the site's own elevation and temperature; no manufacturer power curve is reproduced.
turbine-density-correction.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
turbine-density-correction.editionNote: Power is linear in density and cubic in speed, so the two corrections are applied differently and must not be mixed up. Density falls with altitude and with temperature and both run the same way on a hot summer afternoon at elevation, which is precisely when the grid wants the power most. The practical use is diagnostic: a machine that looks like it is underperforming its curve on a hot day at altitude may be performing exactly as it should, and this correction is what distinguishes a fault from physics. The IEC convention is worth knowing because it is what a performance test uses -- rather than scaling power it scales the measured WIND SPEED by the cube root of the density ratio and reads the standard curve. The two agree where power is roughly cubic in speed and diverge near rated, where the machine is power-limited and density affects only where rated is reached, not the rated value; applying the linear correction to RATED power is wrong. The same ISA relation is what the HVAC air-density calculator uses, so the two agree about the air at a site, against a different reference: a power curve is warranted at 59 degF where standard HVAC air is 70 degF.

assumptions.name: Linear in density, cubic in speed
assumptions.value: and the linear form does not apply above rated

assumptions.name: A performance test scales the speed
assumptions.value: by the cube root of the density ratio, not the power

assumptions.name: Measured pressure beats an elevation estimate
assumptions.value: and humidity has a small further effect not modelled

free-surface-moment.formula: Free surface moment = liquid density x i, with i = l b^3 / 12 the second moment of area of a rectangular liquid surface about its own fore-and-aft centreline (l fore and aft, b across). n equal fore-and-aft compartments give l b^3 / (12 n^2). Identical tanks add. Loss of metacentric height = free surface moment / displacement. Units: lb per cubic foot x ft^4 = ft-lb; divided by lb gives ft.
free-surface-moment.edition: The free surface correction as naval architecture states it: Principles of Naval Architecture (SNAME), intact stability, and standard ship stability texts such as Derrett, Ship Stability for Masters and Mates, cited by name.
free-surface-moment.freeAccess: The second moment of area of a rectangle and one division; no table is reproduced. The n-squared rule follows from the cube: n compartments of breadth b/n give n (b/n)^3 = b^3 / n^2.
free-surface-moment.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
free-surface-moment.editionNote: The depth of liquid does not enter, so a nearly empty wide tank costs as much as a half-full one, provided the surface reaches both sides and stays clear of the tank top and bottom. Breadth is cubed, which is why a centreline bulkhead is worth a factor of four. The tank's position in the vessel does not change the moment. Valid at small angles of heel for rectangular surfaces; a shaped tank needs the builder's tank tables.

assumptions.name: Rectangular surface
assumptions.value: i = l b^3 / 12; a tank of another plan is not this model

assumptions.name: Liquid density
assumptions.value: the liquid in the tank: seawater about 64 lb/cu ft, fresh water 62.4, diesel about 53

assumptions.name: Slack tank
assumptions.value: surface reaches both sides and clears the top and bottom through the heel

assumptions.name: Divisions are watertight
assumptions.value: a swash plate with openings does not divide the surface

opacity-six-minute.formula: block average = the sum of the readings divided by their count, with 24 readings at 15-second intervals making one six-minute block; the readings at a stated peak a block could carry is the limit times the count over that peak.
opacity-six-minute.edition: EPA Method 9 (40 CFR Part 60 Appendix A) by name -- readings at 15-second intervals, 24 to a six-minute block, and the block's ARITHMETIC MEAN compared against the limit. The block sum and the limit are ENTERED. It does not validate the observation conditions (sun position, background, distance and angle are specified by the method and a reading outside them is not valid), the observer's certification and its expiry, the applicable limit or its short-duration exceptions, or whether continuous opacity monitoring data would govern instead.
opacity-six-minute.freeAccess: One arithmetic mean; no method text is reproduced.
opacity-six-minute.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
opacity-six-minute.editionNote: The six-minute block is what makes a short puff and a steady haze different findings. A soot blow producing a very dark plume for thirty seconds contributes two readings to a block of twenty-four and the average can remain compliant; a faint plume that never clears contributes twenty-four readings at a lower value and can exceed the same limit. Operators who judge by the worst moment consistently misread which condition is the violation, so both cases are computed side by side. Method 9's observation conditions are as binding as the arithmetic: a reading taken with the sun in the wrong quadrant or against a bright sky is not a valid reading regardless of what the observer saw, which is why an operator's own observation is not equivalent to a certified one.

assumptions.name: Observation conditions are not validated
assumptions.value: sun position, background, distance and angle are specified by the method

assumptions.name: Certification lapses
assumptions.value: observers recertify on a stated interval and a lapsed reading is not enforceable

assumptions.name: Short-duration exceptions are not applied
assumptions.value: many standards allow one period per hour at a higher opacity

concrete-pump-line-pressure.formula: total pressure = static + friction. Static gradient = unit weight (pcf) / 144, so normal weight concrete is 1.04 psi per foot of rise; friction = equivalent length x the entered loss per 100 ft, with bends counted as an equivalent length each and flexible hose as a multiple of its own length.
concrete-pump-line-pressure.edition: The static and friction components of a concrete pump line by name, with ACI 304.2R for pumping and the pump manufacturer's ratings named. NO FRICTION CHART IS SHIPPED: the loss per 100 ft depends on slump, aggregate, fines, admixtures, temperature and line condition, and published charts give ranges. The limit compared against is the pump's rated CONCRETE pressure, not its hydraulic pressure. ACI 304.2R, the pump manufacturer's ratings, the concrete supplier's mix design, and the contractor's competent person govern.
concrete-pump-line-pressure.freeAccess: A division and a multiplication on a friction value the reader takes off a pumping chart; no chart is reproduced.
concrete-pump-line-pressure.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
concrete-pump-line-pressure.editionNote: The static term is the easy one and often the larger on a high pour: a unit weight in pcf over 144 square inches to the square foot is the pressure gradient per foot of rise, which for normal weight concrete is 1.04, so a fifteen storey lift is more than 150 psi before any friction. Bends and reducers are the quiet killers and are handled the way the field handles them, as equivalent feet of straight line: each 90 degree bend is worth several feet and flexible hose several times its own length, which is why a line threading a congested site hits the pump's limit at a fraction of its nominal reach. The output worth having is the additional line still available, because a crew that discovers the limit by plugging the line loses the pour.

assumptions.name: The friction value is entered
assumptions.value: it depends on slump, aggregate, fines, admixtures, temperature and line condition
assumptions.source: a pumping chart for the mix and line

assumptions.name: Pumpability is a mix question
assumptions.value: a marginal mix blocks regardless of calculated pressure

assumptions.name: Line restraint is not addressed
assumptions.value: a line under pressure that separates whips; couplings and exclusion zones are safety requirements

fiber-strand-count-planning.formula: feeder fibers = ceil(premises/split ratio); distribution fibers = ceil(premises/terminal ports); apply entered spare and round up to the first entered standard cable count.
fiber-strand-count-planning.edition: Outside-plant fiber-count takeoff with user-supplied standard cable counts and costs.
fiber-strand-count-planning.freeAccess: Ceilings, a spare factor, and installed-cost comparison.
fiber-strand-count-planning.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
fiber-strand-count-planning.editionNote: SIZE THE PERMANENT PLANT FOR PREMISES PASSED, NOT INITIAL TAKE RATE. On the worked route, 63 feeder fibers round to 72 without explicit spare and 79 with 25% spare round to 96. The larger cable adds $15,840, or 3.2%, because placement is 84% of the lower-count installed cost and would be paid again to add cable later.

assumptions.name: Standard counts are entered
assumptions.value: positive comma-separated values, rounded upward

assumptions.name: Aggregate planning only
assumptions.value: splitter and terminal geography are not designed

assumptions.name: Costs are entered
assumptions.value: placement method, permitting and restoration are site-specific

plow-route-cycle-time.formula: effective speed = plowing speed / overhead factor; cycle time = route lane-miles / effective speed; accumulation between passes = snowfall rate x cycle time; lane-miles per truck = effective speed x cycle target; trucks = system lane-miles / lane-miles per truck, rounded up.
plow-route-cycle-time.edition: Standard winter maintenance route and fleet sizing relations. The overhead factor is ENTERED from the operation's own route timing records; 1.2 to 1.5 is ordinary.
plow-route-cycle-time.freeAccess: A rate relation and a division rounded up.
plow-route-cycle-time.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
plow-route-cycle-time.editionNote: CYCLE TIME IS THE SERVICE LEVEL AND EVERYTHING ELSE IS BOOKKEEPING -- what a customer experiences is how deep the snow is when the plow returns, which is the snowfall rate times the cycle. THE FLEET SCALES INVERSELY WITH THE TARGET, so on a 300 lane-mile system going from a two-hour to an eighty-minute standard costs 3 more trucks out of 8 (38% more fleet) to buy 1.0 in of accumulation at 1.5 in/h. Stating the trade in inches is what makes it a decision rather than a budget argument. THE OVERHEAD FACTOR CARRIES THE WHOLE ANSWER: the same 30 lane-mile route cycles in 86 minutes at 1.2 and 108 at 1.5, and a fleet sized from the map rather than the route is short. Plowing speed is treated as CONSTANT and is not -- deep or wet snow slows a truck at exactly the moment the cycle matters most -- and route sequencing by priority means the lowest-priority streets cycle far slower than any published standard.

assumptions.name: Overhead factor is entered
assumptions.value: turns, intersections, traffic, blade lifts and reload trips; 1.2 open, 1.5 dense grid
assumptions.source: the operation's own route timing records

assumptions.name: Constant plowing speed
assumptions.value: depth and snow type are not modelled

assumptions.name: No priority sequencing
assumptions.value: every route is treated as cycling on the same standard
assumptions.source: the public works or contract standard

radon-fan-static.formula: pipe velocity = flow / area; friction by Darcy-Weisbach with f = 64 / Re below Re 2,300, the Blasius smooth-pipe factor f = 0.316 / Re^0.25 up to 100,000, and Swamee-Jain above, converted from feet of air to inches of water column; the share divides that loss by the fan's entered static.
radon-fan-static.edition: Duct friction by Darcy-Weisbach on a smooth pipe, with the sub-slab resistance ENTERED as a measured fan static rather than predicted, because it depends on the aggregate, the fines and the soil and is not calculable in advance.
radon-fan-static.freeAccess: Standard duct friction relations and two unit conversions.
radon-fan-static.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
radon-fan-static.editionNote: The share is computed rather than asserted, and the arithmetic does not support the usual description of it. On the standard residential case -- 80 cfm through 30 ft of 4 in PVC against a fan developing 1.2 in wc -- the pipe costs about 0.111 in wc, which is 9% of the system, not the 'percent or two' the rule of thumb claims. The CONCLUSION still holds, because the soil is still around 90% of the resistance and upsizing to 6 in buys back only 0.095 in wc. But 'upsizing the pipe changes almost nothing' is a 3 to 4 times understatement of what it does change, and on a long run with a fan already at its limit that margin is the job. THE DIAGNOSTIC IS VACUUM AGAINST FLOW: high vacuum at low flow is a tight sub-slab and needs MORE SUCTION POINTS; low vacuum at high flow is a short circuit to outdoor air and needs sealing. A bigger fan makes the second worse. And a radon fan is selected from its CURVE, not its rating, because the operating point sits on a system curve nobody knows until the system runs.

assumptions.name: Smooth-pipe friction factor
assumptions.value: Blasius, appropriate to PVC; a corrugated or flexible run is far worse

assumptions.name: Fan static is entered
assumptions.value: the sub-slab resistance is not predictable

assumptions.name: Fittings are not counted
assumptions.value: elbows and the roof termination add to the entered length
